theme.title: Mixed / Stock-Picker's Market
theme.summary: Real Estate (+2.28%) and Health Care (+0.93%) led the market today, while Technology (-0.84%) and Consumer Discretionary (-0.03%) brought up the rear. That split lines up with a rotation out of growth: growth-oriented sectors averaged -0.05% versus +0.67% for defensives and +0.85% for value and cyclicals, suggesting money moved from high-multiple names into steadier, cash-generative businesses. Major indices moved in a tighter band — S&P 500 +0.33%, Dow +0.51%, Nasdaq -0.17% — without one clearly dominating. Small caps moved roughly in line with the broader market, with the Russell 2000 at +0.25%. The VIX fell 4.39% to 17.88, which reads as an orderly rotation rather than panic-driven selling. Gold added 0.96% to $4,069.80, crude oil was little changed at $88.21, and bitcoin slipped 1.73% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
